title: The Vampire Squid Hides in Water Almost Without Oxygen and Eats Marine Snow

scenes.text: A squid that lives where most squid would suffocate.
The vampire squid. It lives 600 to 1,200 metres down, where oxygen can fall below five percent.
Most cephalopods can't go below fifty percent oxygen. This one has a very slow metabolism and a protein that clings to oxygen.
It doesn't hunt. It's the only known cephalopod that doesn't catch live prey. It eats marine snow, falling bits of dead matter.
It catches the drifting crumbs on sticky filaments and rolls them into a ball with mucus.
When threatened, it skips the ink. Its tentacle tips release a sticky glowing cloud that lasts up to ten minutes.

description:
The vampire squid lives at 600 to 1,200 metres in the oxygen minimum zone, where oxygen can be under five percent, and survives with a very low metabolism.
It is the only known cephalopod that does not catch live prey, feeding on marine snow trapped in mucus on its filaments, and it defends itself with bioluminescent mucus that glows for up to ten minutes.
Would you swim down to meet it?
subject: vampire squid
first_comment: A squid that lives on crumbs in the dark. What is the weirdest deep sea animal you know?
